coordinateSystem: Original body-fixed radar-model Cartesian axes; positive Z is the selected spin pole; east-positive longitude; arbitrary display phase
source: Taylor et al. (2007), Science 316, 274–277 and supporting material; Arecibo, Goldstone and NASA/JPL: ecliptic J2000 lambda 180 deg, beta -85 deg, period 0.20290068129070193 h; equatorial conversion uses J2000 obliquity 23.439291111 deg. The archived mesh matches the paper’s A-rough best-fit model to its rounded dimensions and volume. Northern observations constrain the shape better than the southern hemisphere. Rotation uses the published 2001-07-27 reference spin rate of 42582.41 degrees/day, held fixed for display; the measured 0.0002 degrees/day² spin acceleration is not extrapolated. This is not a current attitude ephemeris.
displayPolicy: Hold the published 2001 reference spin rate fixed; arbitrary phase. Do not integrate the measured acceleration to the scene epoch.
